narrative:
The model estimates a 61% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of just 1-5 years was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expected to stay, only about half had similarly limited experience, while many had 6-10 years or more. This limited tenure appears to signal higher turnover risk to the system.

The fact that you have received other job offers while at the company was the second most important factor, pushing the prediction toward leaving. This suggests the model sees external opportunities as a strong indicator that you may depart.

Your time at this specific organization (also 1-5 years) was the third most influential element and further increased the likelihood of leaving. Like your overall experience, this shorter tenure in your current role stands out compared to employees predicted to stay, where over 48% have been with their organization for six years or longer.

Taken together, these elements around your experience level and external opportunities outweighed other positive aspects such as having medical insurance, receiving compensation for overtime, and finding training programs useful.

The organization should consider discussing your career development goals with you directly and exploring ways to strengthen your sense of stability and recognition. You may want to reflect on whether your current role aligns with your longer-term aspirations.
